question: How is the knowledge born of the upper stream characterized in the cited scripture?
premises: The cited teaching addresses the beloved and identifies this knowledge as supreme.
This knowledge arises from the upper stream.
It expresses higher and higher forms of consciousness on the supreme path.
inference: The upper-stream knowledge is supreme because it articulates progressively higher consciousness-forms along the supreme path.
plain_english: ‘O beloved, this knowledge born of the upper stream is that supreme knowledge’—so it is taught by that which expresses higher and higher forms of consciousness on the supreme path.
